meta.subtitle: ARCALYST keeps growing and guidance went up, but the price already assumes the consensus path and the downside case is larger than the expected gain

advisories: model vs Street expected return diverge by 45pp — informational, not scored

analystSentiment.commentary:
Kiniksa is a one-product commercial story. ARCALYST drives essentially all revenue, the second quarter of 2026 grew strongly on the year-ago quarter, and management raised its 2026 ARCALYST net product revenue guidance in the July 28, 2026 release. The pipeline aims to extend the same franchise with more convenient dosing, but its lead candidate is a late-decade launch.

The shares trade at more than double the 52-week low of $35.20 and close to the $82.94 high. At that level the market is paying for the consensus earnings path. Whether operating leverage arrives, given the partner split and rising R&D, is the question the valuation turns on.

We rate KNSA a HOLD. The operating story is sound; the price leaves too little reward for the downside we can construct.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Kiniksa Pharmaceuticals International, plc is a London-based biopharmaceutical company focused on cardiovascular indications. Its commercial product, ARCALYST, is an IL-1 alpha and IL-1 beta cytokine trap licensed from Regeneron in 2017 and approved by the FDA in March 2021 for recurrent pericarditis and reduction in risk of recurrence in adults and children 12 years and older. ARCALYST is also approved in the United States for CAPS and DIRA.

Kiniksa sells and distributes ARCALYST in the United States through a select network of specialty pharmacies and shares ARCALYST profits and third-party proceeds with Regeneron under the license. ARCALYST is currently only approved for sale in the United States, and the company expects to derive substantially all product revenue there for the foreseeable future. Kiniksa reports a single segment.

The pipeline is built around the same IL-1 pathway: KPL-387, a monthly subcutaneous monoclonal antibody in a pivotal Phase 3 trial in recurrent pericarditis, and KPL-1161, a pre-clinical, longer half-life follow-on. Kiniksa has also licensed vixarelimab to Genentech and ARCALYST rights in the Huadong Territory to Huadong.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body:
ARCALYST's growth, high gross margins, cash generation and raised outlook describe a sound business, and the reported numbers support that.

Our HOLD rests on price. The scenario analysis in the valuation section puts the probability-weighted value only modestly above the current price, against a Bear case that sits much further below it, so the reward does not justify a BUY.

catalysts: Third-quarter 2026 results, as a check on whether ARCALYST is tracking toward the raised full-year guidance.
Enrollment progress in PASTORALE, the pivotal Phase 3 trial of KPL-387 in recurrent pericarditis.
Initiation of a first-in-human Phase 1 trial of KPL-1161, which the company expects by the end of 2026.
Any development, regulatory or sales-based milestone from the Genentech vixarelimab license.
risks: Single-product concentration: ARCALYST is the company's one commercial product.
Supply: ARCALYST depends on sole-source third-party manufacturing.
Valuation: the downside case is much larger than the expected gain.
Pipeline timing: the franchise extension is a late-decade launch.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
Total revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $243.6 million, compared to $156.8 million for the second quarter of 2025, a {+ +55.4% YoY +} increase. The company attributes the growth to new and repeat prescribers of ARCALYST, which led to a meaningful increase in patients on therapy.

Costs rose quickly too. Total operating expenses were $216.4 million against $136.6 million a year earlier. Collaboration expenses, which consist mainly of Regeneron's share of ARCALYST profit under the even split, reached $88.1 million against $52.4 million, so the partner's share rises in step with sales. R&D expenses were $40.9 million against $18.8 million, which the company attributes primarily to increased KPL-387 clinical and manufacturing activity and preclinical investment. SG&A was $63.9 million against $46.9 million, attributed to ARCALYST commercialization. As a result, net income of $25.4 million versus $17.8 million grew more slowly than revenue in the quarter, and the Q2'26 operating margin was 11.2%.

On an annual view, FY25 revenue of $677.6M grew +60.1% and the operating margin turned to 11.4% from -10.8% in FY24. Diluted EPS has been uneven, with a spike to $2.60 in FY22 that no source explains. Gross margin has stayed in a high band, at 88.5% in FY25. The quarter shows strong revenue with slower profit growth; whether profit growth catches up is the valuation question taken up below.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
As of June 30, 2026, Kiniksa had $525.9 million of cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments and no debt, according to the second-quarter release. The FY25 year-end figure for cash and short-term investments was $0.4B, so the cash balance has grown during 2026.

Liquidity is ample: the current ratio was 3.79 at FY25 and 3.90 on a trailing basis, and total equity was $0.6B at FY25. The balance sheet funds the pivotal Phase 3 trial and the KPL-1161 program without external capital on today's plan, and we see no balance-sheet risk to the thesis.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow turned meaningful in FY25 at $136.4M, a 20.1% FCF margin, up from single-digit margins of 2.6%, 4.9% and 6.0% in FY22 through FY24. Capital spending is small, so operating cash flow and free cash flow move together. The company expects its current operating plan to remain cash flow positive on an annual basis, and the trailing FCF yield is 3.1%.

One caution applies. Second-quarter 2026 operating expenses included $11.6 million of non-cash, share-based compensation, so cash generation flatters per-share economics somewhat. Even so, the business is self-funding, which we count as a clear positive.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing numbers the shares trade at 77.9x earnings, 53.3x EV/EBITDA and 7.1x sales. The vendor's forward P/E labelled NTM is 65.9x; set against the FY26E consensus EPS of $1.16, that figure is effectively a current-year multiple rather than a true next-twelve-months one. On the FY27E consensus EPS of $1.62 the forward P/E is ~47.2x. It is not stated whether the consensus EPS estimates are on a GAAP or adjusted basis, so we do not label these forward multiples as GAAP. Peer multiples were not available, so we make no relative comparison.

Consensus EPS rises from $0.75 in FY25 through FY26E to FY27E faster than consensus revenue grows, so the estimates assume operating leverage. The second quarter has not yet shown it, because collaboration and R&D costs rose with sales. Even on FY27E the stock carries a high earnings multiple, so a year in which that leverage fails to appear would hit both earnings and the multiple. That is the core of our valuation caution.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: ARCALYST beats a consensus that already sits near the top of guidance, PASTORALE progresses on plan, and the market pays a higher multiple. We anchor to the Street high target of $108.00 over a 12-month horizon.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Consensus is delivered and FY27E EPS of $1.62 stays intact. We anchor to the Street low target of $87.00, which implies a modestly higher multiple of FY27E EPS than today's ~47.2x. We accept that because by the end of a 12-month horizon investors will be pricing growth beyond FY27, and every one of the 8 analysts has a target at or above it.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: FY27 EPS stalls at about the FY26E level of $1.16 instead of growing, and the market derates the stock to a multiple of those earnings below today's forward multiple. Over 12 months that implies about $48.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Each weight maps to a distinct outcome. Base, at 55%, is the strong-execution case: consensus is delivered and the stock settles at the Street low target. Bull, at 25%, needs a beat on top of that and a higher multiple. Bear, at 20%, needs both an earnings stall and a derating. We put Bear below Bull because the company has just raised guidance and expects its plan to stay cash flow positive, so a stall would need a break in current trends. We do not put it lower, because a single disappointing year would likely compress a multiple this high.

The Bear case is a real downside: it sits well below the current price but above the 52-week low of $35.20.

On these weights the expected upside clears the BUY hurdle only narrowly, and reward/risk falls well short of the BUY bar because the Bear price sits much further below the current price than the probability-weighted value sits above it. The call is HOLD, and it is not close on reward/risk; equal weights on the two tails would also give HOLD. The target range brackets the Base case and spans from modestly below the current price to the consensus target of $98.00.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Kiniksa reports one segment, and ARCALYST product revenue is substantially all of it, with FY25 revenue of $677.6M shown as the consolidated total. License and collaboration revenue from Huadong and Genentech is small today: of the $32.0 million Huadong transaction price, $0.2 million had been recognized as of June 30, 2026. The Genentech license could pay up to approximately $600.0 million in contingent payments, of which approximately $570.0 million remains, but those payments are contingent and we place no value on them in our scenarios.

moatFactors.name: Regulatory exclusivity
moatFactors.body: The FDA granted ARCALYST Orphan Drug exclusivity in 2021 for recurrent pericarditis, and the FDA granted KPL-387 Orphan Drug Designation in October 2025. No expiry date is given for these protections, and the 10-K lists the inability to establish and maintain patent and trade secret protection or regulatory exclusivity, and competition from biosimilars, among its commercialization risks.

moatFactors.name: Entrenched prescriber base and long therapy duration
moatFactors.body: Since launch, more than 5,000 prescribers have written ARCALYST prescriptions for recurrent pericarditis, and average total duration of therapy was approximately 3 years as of the end of the second quarter of 2026. Long-duration patients make revenue recurring, but the same 10-K risk list notes that alternative therapies with the same or different mechanisms could compete.

moatFactors.name: Franchise extension in the same indication
moatFactors.body: The Phase 3 antibody targets monthly self-administration in a liquid formulation and KPL-1161 a quarterly profile, against weekly ARCALYST. If they succeed, Kiniksa keeps its patients in-house with more convenient dosing. Both remain investigational, so this factor is a possibility rather than a protection today.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. ARCALYST holds a defined position in a rare indication, with orphan exclusivity, a large prescriber base and long average therapy duration. Against that, the partner split limits Kiniksa's economics, the franchise depends on Regeneron's license and on third-party manufacturers, and no exclusivity end date is given. Durability beyond the current exclusivity window rests on the late-decade launch of the Phase 3 antibody.

points: **Raised guidance.** Kiniksa expects 2026 ARCALYST net product revenue of between $980 million and $995 million, compared to prior guidance of between $930 million and $945 million, per the July 28, 2026 release. FY26E consensus revenue of $993.7M sits near the top of that range, so the Street already assumes strong delivery.

**Penetration headroom.** As of the end of the second quarter of 2026, approximately 21% of the 14,000 multiple-recurrence patients were actively on ARCALYST, and the 10-Q estimates a United States prevalent recurrent pericarditis population of approximately 40,000 patients seeking and receiving treatment. The runway is real, though the company does not say what share it expects to reach.

**KPL-387.** PASTORALE, an event-driven randomized withdrawal study enrolling up to approximately 85 participants, began enrolling and dosing patients after Phase 2 data supported the 300 mg monthly dose. The company expects to begin commercializing the antibody in 2028 or 2029, so it is not a near-term revenue driver, and the release cautions that final data may differ from the interval analysis.

**Next year.** Consensus looks for FY27E revenue of $1.2B, which implies continued growth but slower than this year's pace. Whether ARCALYST can sustain growth as penetration rises is the central question for the stock, and it remains open.

management.leadership: Sanj K. Patel is Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, per the July 28, 2026 release. No tenure or biography is available for him or other officers, so we do not characterize the team's track record beyond the reported results. The commercial and clinical progress covered in the growth section gives a favorable read on execution. The open question is whether the company can carry the same commercial discipline into a second product, which no current data can test.
management.capitalAllocation: The cash flow data show no share repurchases and no dividends in FY21 through FY25, and the dividend yield is 0.00%. Capital goes to the pipeline: higher R&D spending on KPL-387 and KPL-1161, and commercial investment behind ARCALYST. In February 2025 the company announced plans to discontinue development of abiprubart in Sjogren's Disease and to explore strategic alternatives for the asset, which shows some willingness to prune. We consider the reinvestment sensible while ARCALYST funds it, but the forward-looking statements also flag business development as a risk to financial performance, and no deal pipeline is disclosed to assess.
management.governance: According to the proxy statement dated April 16, 2026, all directors other than Sanj K. Patel qualify as independent under Nasdaq listing requirements; Mr. Patel does not because he is the Chief Executive Officer. The proxy states there are no family relationships among directors or executive officers, and that M. Cantey Boyd joined the board in 2024 after a recommendation from an independent director. The combined Chairman and CEO role concentrates authority in one person, which outside holders should weigh against an otherwise independent board.
management.insiderOwnership:
The proxy excerpt dated April 16, 2026 describes four share classes as of its record date: 46,218,660 Class A Shares, 1,795,158 Class B Shares, 12,781,964 Class A1 Shares and 16,057,618 Class B1 Shares. Class A1 and B1 Shares convert one-for-one into Class A Shares on notice, and a conversion that would take a holder above 4.99% of the Class A Shares needs at least sixty-one (61) days' prior notice. The excerpt does not include the ownership table itself, so we cannot attribute stakes to any director, officer or outside holder.

For an outside Class A holder, the A1 and B1 block is a sizeable pool that sits outside the Class A count and can convert into Class A over time, adding to potential supply of the listed shares; the notice requirement gives some warning before large conversions. The vendor's ~78.02M share count is derived from market cap and is on a different basis from the proxy's class-by-class counts; the per-share figures in this report use the vendor's figures.

idiosyncratic: **Single-product dependence.** ARCALYST is Kiniksa's one commercial product and is approved for sale only in the United States. Any slowdown in new patient starts, payor coverage or specialty pharmacy performance would hit revenue directly; the 10-K notes the company currently enjoys largely favorable coverage and seeks to maintain it. Watch quarterly patient and prescriber figures and any change in payor terms.

**Partner economics.** The partner split described in the income discussion caps the profit Kiniksa keeps from each extra dollar of ARCALYST sales, so earnings leverage depends on the company's own cost base. Track collaboration expenses against revenue each quarter.

**Supply.** The 10-K filed February 24, 2026 listed delays in the ongoing technology transfer of ARCALYST drug substance manufacturing as a risk; in June 2026 the FDA approved Samsung Biologics as the replacement contract manufacturer, which addresses that item. What remains, per the July 28, 2026 release, is reliance on third parties as the sole source of supply of drug substance and drug product, so a problem at a single supplier could interrupt sales. Track inventory and supply commentary in future 10-Qs.

**Clinical and regulatory.** PASTORALE could produce negative, inconclusive or commercially uncompetitive results, and regulators could require additional data, per the release's own cautions. A setback would remove the franchise-extension leg of the thesis. Monitor enrollment updates and the KPL-1161 Phase 1 start.

**Competition.** The 10-K lists competitor products, biosimilars and alternative therapies with the same or different mechanisms among commercialization risks. No specific entrant is named, so the risk is unquantified. Follow any new approvals in recurrent pericarditis.
risks.systemic: Drug pricing and reimbursement policy is the main external risk: the forward-looking statements cite current and future healthcare reforms affecting payment for healthcare products, and orphan-disease pricing depends on payor tolerance. The company carries no debt, so interest rate moves affect the shares mainly through the discount rate investors apply. As a London-based company with a United States revenue base, Kiniksa also cites global economic policy uncertainty among its risks.

body: HOLD, with a target range of $70 to $98 over 12 months, for the reasons set out in the valuation section.

We would turn more constructive if the share price fell meaningfully with the consensus path intact, or if 2027 guidance, when issued, comes in clearly above the FY27E consensus revenue. We would turn more cautious if ARCALYST guidance were cut, if a supply problem interrupted sales, or if PASTORALE were delayed.
